summary: The bill requires most aircraft to install collision avoidance systems with audible alerts, revises helicopter routes and air traffic procedures near airports including DCA, mandates controller training and risk assessments, and directs DoD to equip rotary-wing aircraft and update safety management to prevent midair collisions.

scores.thoughts: The bill mandates extensive FAA rulemaking, equipment equipage (ACAS Xa/Xr, collision prevention tech), controller training, route modifications, safety tools, and oversight mechanisms across civil aviation. These requirements will necessitate increased federal appropriations and expenditures by the FAA and DOT to implement and enforce the new safety standards and infrastructure. This directly expands government spending rather than reducing it.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax policy, rates, deductions, credits, or revenue collection mechanisms.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare coverage, delivery, regulation, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, gun ownership, or regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.

Title II imposes multiple new requirements on the Department of Defense, including aviation safety management systems, risk assessments, training, barometric altimeter updates, transponder maintenance, flight data monitoring, and equipage with collision prevention technology on manned rotary wing and other aircraft. These mandates will require increased DoD expenditures and resources for implementation.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental protections, emissions, or regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, school choice, or federal education policy.

The bill includes post-accident/post-incident drug and alcohol testing requirements for air traffic controllers, but these are narrowly tailored to aviation safety enforcement rather than broader drug decriminalization or enforcement policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
The bill contains no provisions related to tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
By mandating new federal spending without offsetting revenue measures, the bill implicitly accepts additional deficit spending rather than prioritizing debt reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.

Section 105 prohibits the use of ADS-B data for revenue identification purposes and limits certain federal uses, providing a narrow privacy protection for aircraft operators. This is tangential and does not constitute broad tech or data regulation.
The bill references collective bargaining representatives of controllers and pilots in consultation requirements but does not alter union rights, worker protections, or employer flexibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or civil rights priorities.
